meta.mechanism: anti-interleukin-1β monoclonal antibody (anti-inflammatory; acts upstream of IL-6 and CRP; no LDL-C lowering)
meta.indication: secondary prevention of recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with prior myocardial infarction and hsCRP >=2 mg/L

n_randomized.quote: involving 10,061 patients with previous myocardial infarction and a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level of 2 mg or more per liter
n_randomized.note: Registry (S4) enrollment 10,066; NEJM FAS 10,061 = 'underwent randomization correctly and received at least one dose'. Arms: placebo 3344, 50 mg 2170, 150 mg 2284, 300 mg 2263 (S1 Table 1).

median_followup.quote: At a median follow-up of 3.7 years, the incidence rate for the primary end point was 4.50 events per 100 person-years in the placebo group
median_followup.note: ≈44 months. Topline press release (S2) said 'The median follow-up time was 3.8 years.' (see open_questions).

primary_endpoint.value: Time to first nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death (MACE-3)
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary efficacy end point was nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Previous myocardial infarction and hsCRP >=2 mg/L despite secondary prevention; exclusions: chronic/recurrent infection, prior cancer (other than basal-cell), immunocompromise, TB risk/HIV, other systemic anti-inflammatory therapy
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: involving 10,061 patients with previous myocardial infarction and a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level of 2 mg or more per liter
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Of 17,482 screened, 57.6% randomized; most common exclusion was hsCRP <2 mg/L (46.0% of excluded).

planned_events.quote: The trial was designed to accrue a total of 1400 primary end-point events across all the groups.
planned_events.note: Also in protocol v09 (S5): '1,400 endpoints are necessary to achieve a power ≥ 90%'. Observed primary events: 535+313+320+322 = 1490.

assumed_rrr.quote: Assuming that all three active doses would result in a primary event rate that was 20% lower than the rate with placebo, we calculated that the trial would have more than 90% power to detect a significantly lower risk with at least one canakinumab dose than with placebo.
assumed_rrr.note: Protocol (S5) Table 9-1: with 20% RRR at all doses, power per dose = 72.0% (300 mg), 80.6% (150 mg), 80.3% (50 mg); 93.6% for at least one dose. Protocol notes the 150 mg dose needed RRR of ~15-16% and 300/50 mg ~17-18% to reach significance.

power.quote: we calculated that the trial would have more than 90% power to detect a significantly lower risk with at least one canakinumab dose than with placebo
power.note: >0.90 for 'at least one dose'; individual-dose power lower (S5 Table 9-1).

alpha.quote: A fixed Bonferroni split of the one sided alpha will be used to account for the two efficacy interim analyses and the final analysis, with a significance level of 0.01% for the first efficacy interim analysis, 0.04% for the second efficacy interim analysis and 2.45% for the final analysis. In this fashion the family-wise type I error rate will be controlled at the one-sided 2.5% level.
alpha.note: Registry protocol document. Final one-sided 2.45% split 20%/40%/40% for 300/150/50 mg; NEJM two-sided thresholds 0.01058 (300 mg) and 0.02115 (50 and 150 mg).

dose_arms.value: placebo; canakinumab 50 mg, 150 mg, 300 mg SC every 3 months (target ratio 1.5:1:1:1)
dose_arms.quote: Initially, patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive placebo, canakinumab at a dose of 150 mg, or canakinumab at a dose of 300 mg. After the enrollment of 741 patients, a 50-mg dose of canakinumab was added at the request of a regulatory agency, and the randomization ratio was adjusted accordingly; we sought to achieve a final randomization ratio of 1.5 (placebo group):1:1:1
dose_arms.note: 300 mg = 300 mg every 2 weeks x2 then every 3 months per NEJM (not extracted verbatim).

multiplicity.value: Closed testing / graphical weighted procedure; two-sided primary-endpoint P thresholds 0.02115 for 50 mg and 150 mg, 0.01058 for 300 mg; key secondary tested only if that dose's primary met threshold
multiplicity.quote: the two-sided P value thresholds for statistical significance for the primary end point were 0.01058 for the test of the 300-mg dose of canakinumab versus placebo and 0.02115 for the tests of the other two doses versus placebo.
multiplicity.note: Consequence: 150 mg (P=0.02075 < 0.02115) significant; 300 mg (HR 0.86, P=0.0314 > 0.01058) NOT significant despite similar HR; 50 mg not significant. Registry (S4) reports one-sided adjusted P: 150 mg 0.0241, 300 mg 0.0648, 50 mg 0.1895 vs significance level 0.0245.

sample_size_change.value: 17,200 planned -> ~10,000 (Amendment 8, Dec 2013), event target unchanged at 1400
sample_size_change.quote: The investigators initially sought to enroll 17,200 patients in order to accrue 1400 events over a period of 5 years. In December 2013, at the request of the sponsor, the sample size was reduced to 10,000 patients.
sample_size_change.note: Protocol (S5) Amendment 8: 'not based on safety or efficacy concerns, instead it resulted from a strategic decision that considered the higher than anticipated primary event endpoint rate'.

stopped_early.quote: enrollment began in April 2011 and was completed in March 2014; the last trial visit was in June 2017.
stopped_early.note: Ran to planned event count; two interim efficacy analyses with tiny alpha (0.01%, 0.04% one-sided) did not stop the trial.

baseline.quote: The median high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level at trial entry was 4.20 mg per liter
and the median LDL cholesterol level was 82.4 mg per deciliter (2.13 mmol per liter).
baseline.note: Table 1 by arm: placebo 82.8, 50 mg 81.2, 150 mg 82.4, 300 mg 83.5, all canakinumab 82.0 mg/dL. 93.4% on lipid-lowering therapy.
Quote reconstructed from table row text; value is the pooled canakinumab column. Overall-population value not given.

biomarker_effects.quote: At 48 months, the median reduction from baseline in the high-sensitivity C-reactive protein level was 26 percentage points greater in the group that received the 50-mg dose of canakinumab, 37 percentage points greater in the 150-mg group, and 41 percentage points greater in the 300-mg group than in the placebo group.

biomarker_effects.method: difference in median percent change from baseline vs placebo; 150 mg q3mo
biomarker_effects.quote: 37 percentage points greater in the 150-mg group

biomarker_effects.method: difference in median percent change from baseline vs placebo; 300 mg q3mo

Similar effects were observed for the interleukin-6 level (measured up to 12 months).

biomarker_effects.quote: the median reductions in C-reactive protein at 4 months were 36.4%, 53.0%, 64.6%, and 58.7% for the 5-, 15-, 50-, and 150-mg canakinumab doses, respectively, compared with 4.7% for placebo (all P values ≤0.02).
biomarker_effects.note: Phase IIb in 556 patients with well-controlled diabetes; value shown is the 50 mg monthly arm; 150 mg monthly -58.7%.

biomarker_effects.method: median percent reduction within arm (NOT placebo-subtracted); placebo -2.9%

No effects were seen for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, or non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, although triglyceride levels increased ≈10% in the 50-mg (P=0.02) and 150-mg (P=0.03) groups.

hr.note: Headline = 150 mg, the only dose meeting the multiplicity threshold. Pooled all doses HR 0.88 (0.79–0.97) (Table 2).

safety_signals.value: fatal infection or sepsis 0.31 vs 0.18 per 100 person-years (pooled canakinumab vs placebo), P=0.02
safety_signals.quote: significantly more deaths were attributed to infection or sepsis in the pooled canakinumab groups than in the placebo group (incidence rate, 0.31 vs. 0.18 events per 100 person-years; P = 0.02)
safety_signals.note: Table 3: placebo 0.18 (23), 50 mg 0.31 (25), 150 mg 0.28 (24), 300 mg 0.34 (29), pooled 0.31 (78); P trend 0.09. Press release S3: 'Fatal infections occurred in about one per 1,000 patients on placebo... higher in the combined ACZ885 group'.

safety_signals.value: neutropenia more common: 0.10 vs 0.06 per 100 person-years (pooled vs placebo)
safety_signals.quote: Neutropenia was more common among patients who were assigned to receive canakinumab than among those in the placebo group

safety_signals.quote: Thrombocytopenia was more common among patients who were assigned to receive canakinumab than among those in the placebo group, but no significant difference in the incidence of hemorrhage was observed.
safety_signals.note: Table 3: pooled 0.60 (150) vs placebo 0.43 (53); P trend 0.02, pooled 0.03.

safety_signals.value: fatal cancer lower: 0.45 vs 0.64 per 100 person-years (pooled vs placebo)
safety_signals.quote: Cancer mortality was significantly lower with canakinumab than with placebo.
safety_signals.note: Table 3: placebo 0.64 (81), 300 mg 0.31 (27), pooled 0.45 (115); P trend <0.001, pooled 0.02. Lung cancer analysis published separately in The Lancet.

safety_signals.value: arthritis, gout and osteoarthritis reduced (gout 0.38 vs 0.80 per 100 person-years)
safety_signals.quote: cana­kinumab resulted in significantly fewer reports of arthritis, gout, and osteoarthritis than did placebo (Table 3).
serious infections were reported in 11.3% vs 10.2% and malignancies were reported in 6.4% vs 7.1% of participants (ACZ885 150mg vs placebo, respectively).

safety_signals.value: Regulatory: FDA complete response letter (Oct 2018) for CV risk reduction sBLA; not approved for CV indication
safety_signals.quote: We received a complete response letter from the FDA in October 2018 regarding our supplemental Biologics License Application for ACZ885 in cardiovascular risk reduction.
safety_signals.location: Novartis Form 20-F FY2018, Item 4 key development projects
safety_signals.note: Nuance: trial 'succeeded' on its primary endpoint but did not lead to a CV approval.

safety_signals.value: Regulatory: EU application withdrawn 2018-12-04; CHMP view that benefits did not outweigh risks
safety_signals.quote: The data provided by the company was not robust enough to clearly demonstrate that canakinumab Novartis is effective in all patients who have had a heart attack.
safety_signals.note: CHMP also: benefits 'were not considered to outweigh the increased risks of serious infections'; questioned the hsCRP-based patient selection and response monitoring. Quotes via WebFetch summary of the EMA page.

genetics.finding: CRP is not causal for CHD: genetically raised CRP not associated with CHD risk (CRP Coronary Heart Disease Genetics Collaboration, 47 studies, 194,418 participants)
genetics.effect: RR 1.00 (0.90–1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised ln CRP vs 1.33 (1.23–1.43) observationally
genetics.quote: In a combined analysis, the risk ratio for coronary heart disease was 1.00 (0.90 to 1.13) per 1 SD higher genetically raised natural log (ln) concentration of C reactive protein.
genetics.note: hsCRP is a marker for patient selection, not the causal mediator. Before readout.

genetics.finding: IL-6 receptor signalling is causal for CHD: IL6R Asp358Ala (rs2228145) raises IL6R and IL-6, lowers CRP and fibrinogen, and lowers CHD risk (IL6R Genetics Consortium / Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration)
genetics.effect: CHD risk -3.4% (1.8–5.0) per 358Ala allele; CRP -7.5% per allele
genetics.quote: For every copy of 358Ala inherited, risk of coronary heart disease was reduced by 3·4% (1·8-5·0).
genetics.note: Supports the IL-1β -> IL-6 -> CRP pathway (canakinumab acts upstream of IL-6). Before readout.

genetics.finding: IL6R MR Consortium (companion paper, same Lancet issue): IL6R rs7529229 (marking Asp358Ala) associated with lower CHD odds
genetics.effect: OR 0.95 (0.93–0.97) per allele, p=1.53e-5; 25,458 cases / 100,740 controls
genetics.quote: the IL6R rs7529229 SNP was associated with a decreased odds of coronary heart disease events (per allele odds ratio 0·95, 95% CI 0·93-0·97, p=1·53×10(-5)).

genetics.finding: TENSION: genetic upregulation of IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL1RN variants, mimicking dual IL-1α/β inhibition such as anakinra) associated with HIGHER CHD risk and higher LDL-C (Interleukin 1 Genetics Consortium)
genetics.effect: CHD OR 1.03 (1.02–1.04) per allele; OR 1.15 (1.08–1.22) for 4 vs 0 IL-1Ra-raising alleles; AAA OR 1.08
genetics.quote: Human genetic data suggest that long-term dual IL-1α/β inhibition could increase cardiovascular risk and, conversely, reduce the risk of development of rheumatoid arthritis.
genetics.note: Published before the CANTOS readout and pointed in the OPPOSITE direction to the CANTOS result. Differences: IL1RN blocks both IL-1α and IL-1β and is lifelong and germline, while canakinumab blocks only IL-1β. Modelling attributed about one third of the association to raised LDL-C. No direct IL1B MR instrument was curated.

consensus_explanation.summary: CANTOS met its primary endpoint at the 150 mg dose (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74-0.98; P=0.02075 vs multiplicity threshold 0.02115). It is widely read as the first proof in humans of the inflammatory hypothesis of atherothrombosis: IL-1β inhibition lowered hsCRP by 26-41 percentage points and IL-6, with no LDL-C change, and reduced recurrent MACE by about 15%. Nuances that make it a qualified success: (1) only one of three doses was formally significant, and the 300 mg dose (HR 0.86) missed its stricter threshold of 0.01058; there was no clear dose-response beyond 150 mg, and the pooled HR was 0.88; (2) the effect was modest and there was no mortality benefit (all-cause HR 0.94); (3) fatal infections or sepsis increased (0.31 vs 0.18 per 100 person-years) and neutropenia increased, while cancer mortality fell; (4) regulators did not approve a CV indication. The FDA issued a complete response letter in Oct 2018, and the EU application was withdrawn on 2018-12-04 after the CHMP judged the benefit modest and not robust and judged that it did not outweigh the infection risk; responder (hsCRP <2 mg/L on treatment) labeling was not accepted; (5) genetics favour IL-6 signalling as the causal mediator (IL6R Asp358Ala MR), not CRP (CRP MR null). IL1RN MR (2015) had suggested that dual IL-1α/β blockade could raise CV risk, which is a tension with the trial result. For forecasting purposes: positive trial, no CV approval.

open_questions: Median follow-up: topline press release (S2, 2017-06-22) says 3.8 years; NEJM (S1) and the Aug 2017 press release (S3) say 3.7 years.

N: registry (S4) enrollment 10,066 vs NEJM 10,061 (NEJM counts patients randomized correctly who received at least one dose; registry FAS excludes misrandomized patients and sites with serious GCP violations).
Baseline LDL-C: NEJM text says median 82.4 mg/dL; Table 1 by-arm values 81.2-83.5 and all-canakinumab 82.0; overall column not shown.
CANTOS IL-6 percent change by dose: NOT FOUND (supplementary tables S1-S5 only).
Whether the Dec 2013 sample size cut (17,200 to 10,000) was publicly disclosed before readout, other than through the registry enrollment target, was not verified.

FDA CRL details (exact date, stated reasons) come from secondary news (TCTMD/Medscape: FDA wanted more data on the hsCRP-responder population); the primary source (S12) states only that a CRL was received in October 2018.

Genetic tension: IL1RN MR (S11) predicts harm from dual IL-1α/β blockade, while CANTOS showed benefit with IL-1β-selective blockade. The consensus reconciliation (IL-1α vs IL-1β, LDL-raising effect, lifelong vs short-term exposure) is not formally established.
